accuracy.evidence: The 20 Hz to 20 kHz human range, and ultrasound above it and infrasound below it, match the AQA GCSE Physics (8463) sound and detection content and the BBC Bitesize GCSE pages. Animal ranges follow the Heffner lab audiograms: dog about 67 Hz to 45 kHz (Heffner 1983), cat about 48 Hz to 85 kHz (Heffner and Heffner 1985), elephant about 16 Hz to 12 kHz (Heffner and Heffner 1982). These are labelled as rough lab values. Age tops (about 19, 15 and 8 kHz at 15, 40 and 70) are marked as typical and varying, in line with NIDCD guidance on presbycusis. Every kHz to Hz conversion was recomputed.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented confusions: ultrasound means very loud (predict on 30 000 Hz, the volume challenge, m3), a silent dog whistle makes no sound (animal-step predict, p3), infrasound and ultrasound are not sound (the tone step's 'still a sound wave' line and the challenge), kHz read as Hz (15 kHz and 0.5 kHz cards, the 20 kHz challenge with ×10 and ×100 traps), and everyone hears the same range (age step predict, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flaghear is built on its own log frequency line from 5 Hz to 200 kHz with infra, audible and ultra zones, overlaid with animal and age hearing bars. The learner hunts for tones inside one range and outside another. No other flagship lab has a hearing-range axis. The pitch and loudness lessons use their own labs, and the shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner drags the tone into all three zones before the text names them. The bars light up to show who hears the chosen tone, so the learner finds that 30 kHz reaches a dog but not a person, that 35 Hz reaches an elephant but not a dog, and that the 70-year-old bar stops first. Each hunt is checked against the real ranges, with a correction that says which way to move.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option. 30 000 Hz is 'very loud' or 'not a sound'. A dog whistle makes 'no sound at all'. A 17 000 Hz tone is heard by 'everyone' or is 'ultrasound'. The next step's dragging and bars settle each one, and A.reveal quotes it back.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own correction. 'Too quiet' is told loudness is not the reason. 15 kHz is told it is 15 000 Hz. 2000 Hz is told kilo means 1000. 'Audible once loud enough' is told volume changes amplitude, not frequency. '17 000 Hz is ultrasound' is told ultrasound starts above 20 000 Hz. The hunt and sort steps also name the slip, for example 'Dogs hear from about 67 Hz. Go lower.'

readability.evidence: The kid paragraphs read at FK grade 2.5 and the adult paragraphs at 7.5 (limits 6.5 and 9.5). The adult text was rewritten from 11.4 by splitting long sentences. Precise terms are used: frequency, hertz, kilohertz, pitch, amplitude, hearing range, infrasound, ultrasound, echolocation, presbycusis.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed, and overlap with the pitch, frequency and wave lessons is under 12 percent. The kid paragraphs cover four separate ideas: what frequency is, the range and its names, unit conversion, and animals and age. The family tip is a concrete, low-volume tone-sweep test at home.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark for every step and after Show me. The frequency line and its 10/100/1k/10k/100k ticks are readable, and the marker was moved above the band after the first screenshots showed it covering the tick labels. The four animal bars and three age bars carry labels inside them, the use card wraps, and the two or three sort zones fit across with large tap areas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13. Every Show me finished, the challenge rendered, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark, and there were no console or page errors. The drag has button twins (Lower, Higher, Check this tone), the sorts have zone buttons, and the canvas aria-label states the tone and who hears it, for example '30 kHz (30 000 Hz). Heard by: Dog, Cat.'
